source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Home INR testing removes the need for clinician review because the device automatically determines and changes the warfarin dose.","B":"Trained, selected clients can test INR at home, but results and warfarin management still require an agreed clinical follow-up plan.","C":"Home INR testing is intended for direct-acting oral anticoagulants rather than for clients receiving long-term warfarin therapy.","D":"Home INR testing is used only when standard laboratory INR testing is unavailable and is otherwise inappropriate for warfarin therapy."}}
source_row.rationale: Home INR self-testing devices allow eligible, appropriately trained and selected clients on long-term warfarin therapy to monitor their own INR more conveniently and potentially more frequently, which for suitable candidates may improve anticoagulation control, though results should still be communicated to and reviewed with the healthcare provider for dose management decisions.
source_row.source_detail: FDA home INR guidance: know target INR and testing schedule, contact provider for out-of-range results, and periodically compare meter results with a laboratory method. Current FDA device guidance reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
